chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā Ibrāhīm Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, upon them both be peace:
About a man who is traveling, then arrives and enters the houses of al-Kūfah: should he perform the salat (prayer) in full, or should he remain shortening it until he enters to his family?
He said: “Rather, he remains shortening it until he enters to his family.”

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: his family or household, marking the point of actual arrival home
key_terms.أَيُتِمُّ: does he complete fully, meaning perform the prayer in full length
key_terms.بُيُوتَ الْكُوفَةِ: the houses or residential boundary of al-Kūfah
key_terms.مُسَافِرًا: a traveler, one in the state of travel
key_terms.مُقَصِّرًا: shortening, meaning performing the traveler’s reduced prayer

ai.seo_question: When does a returning traveler stop shortening salat (prayer) and begin praying in full?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about salat (prayer) during travel upon returning home. It states that a traveler continues to perform shortened prayer even after entering the houses of al-Kūfah, until he actually enters to his family.
